or.name: or
or.title: Boolean Or
or.description: The or function returns the symbol TRUE if any of its arguments evaluates to the symbol TRUE; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE. Each argument of the function is evaluated from left to right.

and.name: and
and.title: Boolean And
and.description: The and function returns the symbol TRUE if each of its arguments evaluates to the symbol TRUE; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE. Each argument of the function is evaluated from left to right.

not.name: not
not.title: Boolean Not
not.description: The not function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument evaluates to the symbol FALSE; otherwise it returns the symbol FALSE.

send.name: send
send.title: Manipulating Instances
send.description: Objects are manipulated by sending them messages.

make-instance.name: make-instance
make-instance.title: Creating Instances
make-instance.description: Like facts, instances of user-defined classes must be explicitly created by the user.

active-make-instance.name: active-make-instance
active-make-instance.title: Creating Instances
active-make-instance.description: Like facts, instances of user-defined classes must be explicitly created by the user.

initialize-instance.name: initialize-instance
initialize-instance.title: Reinitializing Existing Instances
initialize-instance.description: The initialize-instance function provides the ability to reinitialize an existing instance with class defaults and new slot-overrides.

bind.name: bind
bind.title: Binding Variables
bind.description: The bind function allows values to be assigned to variables.

object-pattern-match-delay.name: object-pattern-match-delay
object-pattern-match-delay.title: Delayed Pattern-Matching When Manipulating Instances
object-pattern-match-delay.description: While creating, modifying, or deleting instances, the object-pattern-match-delay function delays pattern-matching activities for rules until after all of the manipulations have been made.

modify-instance.name: modify-instance
modify-instance.title: Directly Modifying an Instance with Delayed Pattern-Matching
modify-instance.description: The modify-instance function uses the direct-modify message to change the values of the instance.

active-modify-instance.name: active-modify-instance
active-modify-instance.title: Directly Modifying an Instance with Immediate Pattern-Matching
active-modify-instance.description: The active-modify-instance function uses the direct-modify message to change the values of the instance.

message-modify-instance.name: message-modify-instance
message-modify-instance.title: Modifying an Instance using Messages with Delayed Pattern-Matching
message-modify-instance.description: The message-modify-instance function uses the message-modify message to change the values of the instance.

active-message-modify-instance.name: active-message-modify-instance
active-message-modify-instance.title: Modifying an Instance using Messages with Immediate Pattern-Matching
active-message-modify-instance.description: The active-message-modify-instance function uses the message-modify message to change the values of the instance.

duplicate-instance.name: duplicate-instance
duplicate-instance.title: Directly Duplicating an Instance with Delayed Pattern-Matching
duplicate-instance.description: The duplicate-instance function uses the direct-duplicate message to change the values of the instance.

active-duplicate-instance.name: active-duplicate-instance
active-duplicate-instance.title: Directly Duplicating an Instance with Immediate Pattern-Matching
active-duplicate-instance.description: The active-duplicate-instance function uses the direct-duplicate message to change the values of the instance.

message-duplicate-instance.name: message-duplicate-instance
message-duplicate-instance.title: Duplicating an Instance using Messages with Delayed Pattern-Matching
message-duplicate-instance.description: The message-duplicate-instance function uses the message-duplicate message to change the values of the instance.

active-message-duplicate-instance.name: active-message-duplicate-instance
active-message-duplicate-instance.title: Duplicating an Instance using Messages with Immediate Pattern-Matching
active-message-duplicate-instance.description: The active-message-duplicate-instance function uses the message-duplicate message to change the values of the instance.

return.name: return
return.title: Return
return.description: The return function immediately terminates the currently executing deffunction, generic function method, message-handler, defrule, or fact/instance set query function.

any-instancep.name: any-instancep
any-instancep.title: Testing if Any Instance-set Satisfies a Query
any-instancep.description: The any-instancep function applies a query to each instance-set that matches the template.

find-instance.name: find-instance
find-instance.title: Determining the First Instance-set Satisfying a Query
find-instance.description: The find-instance function applies a query to each instance-set that matches the template.

find-all-instances.name: find-all-instances
find-all-instances.title: Determining All Instance-sets Satisfying a Query
find-all-instances.description: The find-all-instances function applies a query to each instance-set that matches the template.

do-for-instance.name: do-for-instance
do-for-instance.title: Executing an Action for the First Instance-set Satisfying a Query
do-for-instance.description: The do-for-instance function applies a query to each instance-set that matches the template.

do-for-all-instances.name: do-for-all-instances
do-for-all-instances.title: Executing an Action for All Instance-sets Satisfying a Query
do-for-all-instances.description: The do-for-all-instances function applies a query to each instance-set that matches the template.

delayed-do-for-all-instances.name: delayed-do-for-all-instances
delayed-do-for-all-instances.title: Executing a Delayed Action for All Instance-sets
delayed-do-for-all-instances.description: Satisfying a Query The delayed-do-for-all-instances function is similar to do-for-all-instances function except that it groups all instance-sets that satisfy the query into an intermediary multifield value.

type.name: type
type.title: Type Determination
type.description: The type function returns a symbol which is the name of the type (or class) of its argument.

numberp.name: numberp
numberp.title: Testing For Numbers
numberp.description: The numberp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is a float or integer; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

floatp.name: floatp
floatp.title: Testing For Floats
floatp.description: The floatp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is a float; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

integerp.name: integerp
integerp.title: Testing For Integers
integerp.description: The integerp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is an integer; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

lexemep.name: lexemep
lexemep.title: Testing For Strings Or Symbols
lexemep.description: The lexemep function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is a string or symbol; otherwise.

stringp.name: stringp
stringp.title: Testing For Strings
stringp.description: The stringp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is a string; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

symbolp.name: symbolp
symbolp.title: Testing For Symbols
symbolp.description: The symbolp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is a symbol; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

evenp.name: evenp
evenp.title: Testing For Even Numbers
evenp.description: The evenp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is an even number; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

oddp.name: oddp
oddp.title: Testing For Odd Numbers
oddp.description: The oddp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is an odd number; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

multifieldp.name: multifieldp
multifieldp.title: Testing For Multifield Values
multifieldp.description: The multifieldp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is a multifield value; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

pointerp.name: pointerp
pointerp.title: Testing For External-Addresses
pointerp.description: The external-addressp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is an external-address; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

external-addressp.name: external-addressp
external-addressp.title: Testing For External-Addresses
external-addressp.description: The external-addressp function returns the symbol TRUE if its argument is an external-address; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE.

eq.name: eq
eq.title: Comparing for Equality
eq.description: The eq function returns the symbol TRUE if its first argument is equal in value to all its subsequent arguments; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE. Note that eq compares types as well as values.

neq.name: neq
neq.title: Comparing for Inequality
neq.description: The neq function returns the symbol TRUE if its first argument is not equal in value to all its subsequent arguments; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE. Note that neq compares types as well as values.

=.title: Comparing Numbers for Equality
=.description: The = function returns the symbol TRUE if its first argument is equal in value to all its subsequent arguments; otherwise it returns the symbol FALSE. Note that = compares only numeric values and will convert integers to floats when necessary for comparison.

<>.title: Comparing Numbers for Inequality
<>.description: The <> function returns the symbol TRUE if its first argument is not equal in value to all its subsequent arguments; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE. Note that <> compares only numeric values and will convert integers to floats when necessary for comparison.

>.title: Greater Than Comparison
>.description: The > function returns the symbol TRUE if for all its arguments, argument n-1 is greater than argument n; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE. Note that > compares only numeric values and will convert integers to floats when necessary for comparison.

>=.title: Greater Than or Equal Comparison
>=.description: The >= function returns the symbol TRUE if for all its arguments, argument n-1 is greater than or equal to argument n; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE. Note that >= compares only numeric values and will convert integers to floats when necessary for comparison.

<.title: Less Than Comparison
<.description: The < function returns the symbol TRUE if for all its arguments, argument n-1 is less than argument n; otherwise it returns the symbol FALSE. Note that < compares only numeric values and will convert integers to floats when necessary for comparison.

<=.title: Less Than or Equal Comparison
<=.description: The <= function returns the symbol TRUE if for all its arguments, argument n-1 is less than or equal to argument n; otherwise, it returns the symbol FALSE. Note that <= compares only numeric values and will convert integers to floats when necessary for comparison.

create$.name: create$
create$.title: Creating Multifield Values
create$.description: The create$ function appends any number of fields together to create a multifield value.

nth$.name: nth$
nth$.title: Specifying an Element
nth$.description: The nth$ function will return a specified field from a multifield value.

member$.name: member$
member$.title: Finding an Element
member$.description: The member$ function determines whether a primitive value is contained in a multifield value.

subsetp.name: subsetp
subsetp.title: Comparing Multifield Values
subsetp.description: The subsetp function checks if one multifield value is a subset of another (i.e., if all the fields in the first multifield value are also in the second multifield value).

delete$.name: delete$
delete$.title: Deletion of Fields in Multifield Values
delete$.description: The delete$ function deletes the specified range from a multifield value.

explode$.name: explode$
explode$.title: Creating Multifield Values from Strings.
explode$.description: The explode$ function constructs a multifield value from a string by using each field in a string as a field in a new multifield value.

implode$.name: implode$
implode$.title: Creating Strings from Multifield Values
implode$.description: The implode$ function creates a single string from a multifield value.

subseq$.name: subseq$
subseq$.title: Extracting a Sub-sequence from a Multifield Value
subseq$.description: The subseq$ function extracts a specified range from a multifield value and returns a new mul- tifield value containing just the sub-sequence.

replace$.name: replace$
replace$.title: Replacing Fields within a Multifield Value
replace$.description: The replace$ function replaces a range of field in a multifield value with a series of single-field and/or multifield values and returns a new multifield value containing the replacement values within the original multifield value.

insert$.name: insert$
insert$.title: Inserting Fields within a Multifield Value
insert$.description: The insert$ function inserts a series of single-field and/or multifield values at a specified location in a multifield value with and returns a new multifield value containing the inserted values within the original multifield value.

first$.name: first$
first$.title: Getting the First Field from a Multifield Value
first$.description: The first$ function returns the first field of a multifield value as a multifield value

rest$.name: rest$
rest$.title: Getting All but the First Field from a Multifield Value
rest$.description: The rest$ function returns all but the first field of a multifield value as a multifield value.

length$.name: length$
length$.title: Determining the Number of Fields in a Multifield Value
length$.description: The length$ function returns an integer indicating the number of fields contained in a multifield value.

delete-member$.name: delete-member$
delete-member$.title: Deleting Specific Values within a Multifield Value
delete-member$.description: The delete-member$ function deletes specific values contained within a multifield value and returns the modified multifield value.

replace-member$.name: replace-member$
replace-member$.title: Replacing Specific Values within a Multifield Value
replace-member$.description: The replace-member$ function replaces specific values contained within a multifield value and returns the modified multifield value.

union$.name: union$
union$.title: Creating the Union of Multifield Values
union$.description: The union$ function creates a multifield value containing a single occurrence of each value contained within each of its multifield arguments.

intersection$.name: intersection$
intersection$.title: Creating the Intersection of Multifield Values
intersection$.description: The intersection$ function creates a multifield value containing a single occurrence of each value that is contained within all of its multifield arguments.

difference$.name: difference$
difference$.title: Creating the Difference of Multifield Values
difference$.description: The difference$ function creates a multifield value containing a single occurrence of each value that is contained within its first argument, but none of its subsequent multifield arguments.

str-cat.name: str-cat
str-cat.title: String Concatenation
str-cat.description: The str-cat function will concatenates its arguments into a single string.

sym-cat.name: sym-cat
sym-cat.title: Symbol Concatenation
sym-cat.description: The sym-cat function will concatenate its arguments into a single symbol.

sub-string.name: sub-string
sub-string.title: Taking a String Apart
sub-string.description: The sub-string function will retrieve a portion of a string from another string.

str-index.name: str-index
str-index.title: Searching a String
str-index.description: The str-index function will return the position of a string inside another string.

eval.name: eval
eval.title: Evaluating a Function within a String
eval.description: The eval function evaluates the string as though it were entered at the Read-Eval-Print Loop (REPL).

build.name: build
build.title: Evaluating a Construct within a String
build.description: The build function evaluates the string as though it were entered at the REPL. The only argument is the construct to be added.

upcase.name: upcase
upcase.title: Converting a String to Uppercase
upcase.description: The upcase function will return a string or symbol with uppercase alphabetic characters.

lowcase.name: lowcase
lowcase.title: Converting a String to Lowercase
lowcase.description: The lowcase function will return a string or symbol with lowercase alphabetic characters.

str-compare.name: str-compare
str-compare.title: Comparing Two Strings
str-compare.description: The str-compare function will compare two strings lexicographically to determine their logical relationship (i.e., equal to, less than, greater than).

str-length.name: str-length
str-length.title: Determining the Length of a String
str-length.description: The str-length function returns the integer length of a string.

check-syntax.name: check-syntax
check-syntax.title: Checking the Syntax of a Construct or Function Call within a String
check-syntax.description: The check-syntax function allows the text representation of a construct or function call to be checked for syntax and semantic errors.

string-to-field.name: string-to-field
string-to-field.title: Converting a String to a Field
string-to-field.description: The string-to-field function parses a string and converts its contents to a primitive data type.

str-replace.name: str-replace
str-replace.title: Replacing Portions of a String
str-replace.description: The str-replace function will replace all occurrences of a sequence of characters in a string with another sequence of characters.

str-byte-length.name: str-byte-length
str-byte-length.title: Determining the Byte Length of a String
str-byte-length.description: The str-byte-length function returns an integer indicating the number of bytes used to represent a string.

open.name: open
open.title: Opening a File
open.description: The open function allows a user to open a file and associate a logical name with it.

close.name: close
close.title: Closing a File
close.description: The close function closes a file stream previously opened with the open command.

printout.name: printout
printout.title: Printing
printout.description: The printout function allows output to a destination associated with a logical name.

print.name: print
print.title: Printing
print.description: The printout function allows output to a destination associated with a logical name.

println.name: println
println.title: Printing
println.description: The printout function allows output to a destination associated with a logical name.

read.name: read
read.title: Reading a Single Field
read.description: The read function allows the input of a single field from a source associated with a logical name.

readline.name: readline
readline.title: Reading an Entire Line
readline.description: The readline function is similar to the read function, but it reads an entire line of input instead of a single field.

format.name: format
format.title: Formatted Printing
format.description: The format function allows formatted output to be sent to a destination associated with a logical name.

rename.name: rename
rename.title: Renaming a File
rename.description: The rename function is used to change the name of a file.

remove.name: remove
remove.title: Removing a File
remove.description: The remove function is used to delete a file.

get-char.name: get-char
get-char.title: Reading a Character
get-char.description: The get-char function allows a single character to be retrieved from an input source.

unget-char.name: unget-char
unget-char.title: Unreading a Character
unget-char.description: The unget-char function allows a single character to be returned to an input source.

read-number.name: read-number
read-number.title: Reading a Number
read-number.description: The read-number function allows input of a single number using the localized format (if one has been specified using the set-locale function).

set-locale.name: set-locale
set-locale.title: Setting the Locale
set-locale.description: The set-locale function allows the locale to be specified which affects the numeric format behavior of the format and read-number functions.

flush.name: flush
flush.title: Flushing Output
flush.description: The flush function writes pending output to a file stream previously opened with the open com- mand.

rewind.name: rewind
rewind.title: Rewinding the File Position
rewind.description: The rewind function sets the position in a file stream previously opened with the open command to the beginning of the file.

tell.name: tell
tell.title: Retrieving the File Position
tell.description: The tell function returns the current position in a file stream previously opened with the open command.

seek.name: seek
seek.title: Setting the File Position
seek.description: The seek function sets the current position in a file stream previously opened with the open command.

chdir.name: chdir
chdir.title: Changing the Current Directory
chdir.description: The chdir function changes the current directory.

with-open-file.name: with-open-file
with-open-file.title: Opening a File Temporarily to Perform Actions
with-open-file.description: The with-open-file function allows users to temporarily open a file, perform actions, and automatically close it once those actions are completed.

+.title: Addition
+.description: The + function returns the sum of its arguments.

-.title: Subtraction
-.description: The - function returns the value of the first argument minus the sum of all subsequent arguments.

*.title: Multiplication
*.description: The * function returns the product of its arguments.

/.title: Division
/.description: The / function returns the value of the first argument divided by each of the subsequent arguments.

div.title: Integer Division
div.description: The div function returns the value of the first argument divided by each of the subsequent arguments.

min.name: min

min.description: The min function returns the value of its smallest numeric argument.

abs.name: abs
abs.title: Absolute Value

float.description: The float function converts its only argument (which should be a numeric expression) to type float and returns this value.

integer.name: integer
integer.title: Convert To Integer
integer.description: The integer function converts its only argument (which should be a numeric expression) to type integer and returns this value.

acos.name: acos

cos.description: The cos function returns the cosine of its argument.
